I am 78 years old, and I have worked my 4.1 mu in Quzhou County for 55 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and I know that wheat needs nitrogen and cotton needs potassium, but most of what I know comes from doing it with my own hands and watching what happens in my fields and my neighbors' fields.

My land is small, so every bag of fertilizer and every hour of labor matters. It is just me and my wife now. I cannot afford to gamble on new methods, but I also know that starving the crops is worse than wasting a little fertilizer. A bad harvest means disaster for us; a few extra yuan on urea is just a cost.

This year I am planting 3.1 mu as wheat-maize double crop and keeping 1 mu in cotton. I cut the cotton back because at my age it is hard to pick, and the bollworms have been trouble, but 1 mu is still worth it for the cash.

For the winter wheat, I will sow Jimai 22. That is an improved variety my neighbor Lao Wang grew last year and he got a good yield. I sow about 25 jin of seed per mu. Before sowing in October, I rotary till the field and spread 80 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as the base. At green-up in March, I topdress with 30 jin of urea per mu, and at jointing I add another 10 jin. That comes to about 30 jin of nitrogen per mu total. I irrigate three times from my well: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I spray twice, once for weeds and once for insects. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the frost does not hit.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed right after the wheat harvest in June. There is no time to plow, so I no-till plant into the wheat stubble. I use about 5 jin of seed per mu. At sowing I put down 60 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, then at the big trumpet stage I spread 30 jin of urea. I irrigate twice, and spray twice for weeds and corn borer. Maize usually gives me about 520 kg per mu.

For the cotton, I deep plough that 1 mu in spring because cotton roots need loose soil. I plant an improved variety, about 6 jin of seed per mu. I apply 60 jin of compound fertilizer as a base. At flowering I topdress with 20 jin of urea, and at the boll stage I add 10 jin of potassium sulfate because cotton drops its bolls without enough potassium. I irrigate three times and spray four times for bollworm — you cannot skip sprays on cotton. I hope to get 220 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I am doing almost the same as last year. That is how I farm.
